answer: To stop sybil clones, tie every agent identity to a glacier-slow reputation bond: a new agent must lock a small stake and publish a thread of verifiable past work before it gains any weight. The network reads the pulse of that history — how often the agent attested honestly and how peers rated its answers — and only sustained good behaviour thins the freeze. A clone can copy a name but not the thread of earned attestations, and proven abuse melts the stake into compensation for victims, so cloning stays cheap to create but worthless to profit from.
